question.worked_solution:
Let us consider the *squared* distance $S$ between $(2,-\frac{7}{2})$ and a general point $P(x,y)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =(x-2)^{2}+{(y+\frac{7}{2})}^{2} \\  & ={x}^{2}-4x+4+{y}^{2}+7y+\frac{49}{4} \\  & ={x}^{2}-4x+{y}^{2}+7y+\frac{65}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We require that the point $P$ lies on the curve $y={x}^{2}-4x.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}S(y) & =y+{y}^{2}+7y+\frac{65}{4} \\  & ={y}^{2}+8y+\frac{65}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the minimum distance, we take the first derivative of $S(y)$ and equate it to zero. This gives the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(y)=2y+8 & =0 \\ 2y & =-8 \\ y & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(y)=2>0.$ Therefore, $y=-4$ is a minimum of $S.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) is minimized when $y=-4.$
